verdicts.reason: A: the two rule lines cut straight through the bottom of the oversized logo glyph and run out past the white panel onto the background. The logo also dwarfs the small 'Calligraphy' headline, which sits low with dead space above it, so the hierarchy is inverted. B: the logo sits directly on the busy watercolour butterfly, the two rule lines are tiny dashes floating at the top with nothing to frame, and the white panel stops short of the right edge, which looks arbitrary. Still, B's headline block is larger, better grouped and reads in a cleaner order, so B is the slightly less bad of the two.
